design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which eligible poor responders were allocated to transdermal testosterone or identical placebo gel using an allocation sequence generated by a random permutation table (blocks of four).

domain_judgments.rationale: A genuine random sequence (permuted blocks) with identical placebo gel was used and most baseline variables were balanced, but allocation concealment is not explicitly described (sequential numbering by a single enrolling physician with small blocks is potentially predictable) and one baseline imbalance (duration of infertility) was observed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "For randomization, the allocation sequence was generated by a random permutation table (blocks of four). Women were enrolled by only one physician (N.M.), who assigned consecutive numbers to women, by order of inclusion." ... "The duration of infertility was longer in the treatment group (P ≤ 0.006). The imbalance in this latter criterion was unexpected."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers and the ultrasonographer were blinded by an identical placebo gel and stimulation protocols were standardized within women, but the authors explicitly used a per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis with asymmetric exclusions (3 testosterone vs 1 placebo), including an investigator-driven discontinuation for absent ovarian desensitization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A paired per protocol analysis was performed." ... "In each group, one patient stopped treatment for personal reasons. In the testosterone-treated group, two patients were discontinued by investigator decision."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although 49/53 randomized women entered the stimulation analysis, the primary outcome (number of oocytes retrieved) was only available for 36 women because of cycle cancellations that were more frequent (though non-significantly) in the testosterone arm, and cancellation is itself outcome-related, so bias from missingness cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Criteria for HCG administration were met, and oocyte retrievals were performed in 16 women treated with testosterone (67%) and in 20 women treated with placebo (80%) (P = 0.45)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (oocyte count) is objective and measured identically in both arms, follicle counts were done by a single blinded sonographer, and hormonal assays were standardized with reported sensitivities and CVs.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Ultrasonography was performed with a 6-MHz vaginal sonde using Toshiba SSA-340A by the same physician (I.C.-D.), who was not informed of patients' treatment allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary endpoint, a priori sample-size calculation and CONSORT flow diagram are reported, but there is no mention of a protocol registration, the planned analysis was changed/supplemented (per-protocol paired within-woman comparisons plus multiple subgroup follicle-size analyses), and the trial was under-recruited relative to the planned 28 per group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary endpoint was the total number of retrieved oocytes. The secondary endpoints were the number of developing follicles, the plasma E levels at HCG day, the total FSH dose, the numbers of metaphase II (MII) oocytes and embryos and the cancellation rate."

overall_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial has a sound outcome measurement approach (objective oocyte counts, blinded sonographer), but concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment plus a baseline imbalance, a per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis with asymmetric exclusions, substantial outcome-related cycle cancellations (only 36/49 reaching retrieval), and the absence of prospective protocol registration in an under-recruited (hence underpowered) null trial. No single domain was judged high, so the overall rating is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: The paper reports a parallel-group randomized clinical trial in which 62 previous low-responder IVF patients were allocated to two stimulation protocols using "a computer-generated randomization table" with "Sealed envelopes for the randomization list", and is registered (NCT00693108).

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated randomization sequence with sealed envelopes was used and baseline characteristics (age, BMI, infertility cause/duration, basal FSH/LH/E2, antral follicle count) were closely similar between groups, consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were allocated to each group according to a computer-generated randomization table. Sealed envelopes for the randomization list were used."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label (no blinding of patients or clinicians) and the comparator differed in multiple co-interventions (minidose GnRH agonist plus higher-dose hMG/FSH), with gonadotrophin dosing adjusted individually from Day 5 by unblinded clinicians, which could influence cancellation/hCG decisions; all randomized patients did receive allocated intervention and were analysed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The study by Massin et al. (2006), but not ours, was a double-blind study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (low response, cycle cancellation, ovum retrieval) rest on ultrasound follicle counts and clinician decisions to cancel or trigger, made by unblinded assessors, although cancellation criteria were explicit and objective, limiting but not removing the potential for influence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "any potential bias, if any, related to the unblinded design of this study seems negligible"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 62 randomized patients with no reported attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The remaining 62 patients were randomized and received appropriate allocated intervention and were thus available for the final analysis of results."

domain_judgments.rationale: A primary end-point and sample-size calculation are pre-specified and the trial is registered, but registration appears retrospective (NCT00693108 registered 2008 for a 2006–2007 trial), no protocol is available, many secondary outcomes are reported, and post-randomization FSH subgroup analyses are emphasized in the abstract conclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Although the division between normal and elevated FSH was done after the randomization and therefore introduces a non-truly randomized comparison..."

overall_summary: Randomization was adequate (computer-generated sequence, sealed envelopes, balanced baselines) with complete outcome data, but the trial was open-label with a comparator differing in several co-interventions and clinician-driven dosing/cancellation decisions, and reporting relies on apparently retrospective registration with emphasized post-randomization subgroup analyses. These issues yield 'some concerns' overall rather than low risk.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a prospective, randomized, single-blind clinical trial in which 50 poor responders were allocated to testosterone pretreatment or no pretreatment "according to a computer-generated randomization list" (NCT01961336).

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence was used and baseline characteristics were balanced (Table I), but the mechanism of allocation concealment (e.g., sealed opaque envelopes, central allocation) is not described, leaving the possibility of foreknowledge of upcoming assignments by the allocating nurse.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were allocated by a study nurse to either testosterone pretreatment for 21 days (n = 26) or no pretreatment (n = 24), according to a computer-generated randomization list."

domain_judgments.rationale: An appropriate ITT analysis was used and key outcome personnel were blinded, but the control group received no placebo gel so patients (and treating clinicians prescribing stimulation) were necessarily aware of allocation, creating potential for co-intervention differences, although stimulation protocol and gonadotrophin dose were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Physicians and embryologists involved in oocyte retrieval and embryo culture were not aware of patient allocation." / "Intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis was performed, analyzing patients according to their randomization."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for essentially all randomized patients (cancellations counted as zero in the ITT analysis), a CONSORT flow diagram is provided, and ITT and per-protocol analyses gave concordant results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Using per protocol analysis, excluding the three patients who did not have oocyte retrieval (as shown in the flow diagram—Fig. 1), the median (interquartile range) of COCs retrieved did not change the direction of the results obtained"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (number of COCs retrieved) is an objective count measured identically in both arms by assessors blinded to allocation, as were the downstream embryological and live-birth outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Physicians and embryologists involved in oocyte retrieval and embryo culture were not aware of patient allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered before enrolment, with a pre-specified single primary outcome, an a priori sample size calculation, and comprehensive reporting of all listed secondary outcomes including null findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "trial registration number: NCT01961336. trial registration date: 10 October 2013. date of first patient's enrollment: 02/2014." / "The primary outcome measure was the number of COCs retrieved."

overall_summary: This prospectively registered RCT had an objective blinded primary outcome, near-complete follow-up and a pre-specified ITT analysis, but allocation concealment procedures are not described and the control arm received no placebo gel, so patients and treating clinicians were unblinded. These two domains ("some concerns" each) drive an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports random allocation of 110 low responders to TTG pretreatment or control using sealed envelopes and a computer-generated randomization list ("Patients were randomly allocated into TTG pretreatment group (n 55) or control group (n 55) by the use of sealed envelopes and a computer-generated list").

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence was used and baseline characteristics were balanced, but the allocation sequence was reportedly "provided to the investigating physicians" and envelopes are not described as opaque/sequentially numbered, raising doubt about concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomly allocated into TTG pretreatment group (n 55) or control group (n 55) by the use of sealed envelopes and a computer-generated list. The sequence of allocation to the two groups was provided to the investigating physicians, and randomization was performed as planned according to the randomization list order."

domain_judgments.rationale: Open-label design with no placebo gel means clinicians knew assignment while making co-intervention decisions (rhFSH dose adjustments every 3–4 days, timing of hCG, cycle cancellation), and no intention-to-treat analysis plan is described, although all 110 randomized cycles appear to be accounted for.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In the present randomized study, the clinicians managing the subjects were not blinded. The lack of blinding of the investigators may have influenced the study results."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for essentially all randomized patients (55 vs 55 initiated cycles analyzed, with only 1 and 2 cancelled cycles reported and included in per-cycle-initiated denominators).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The TTG pretreatment and control groups each consisted of 55 cycles initiated, corresponding to 55 patients... There was no significant difference in overall cycle cancellation rate between the TTG pretreatment and control groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes such as live birth and pregnancy are objective, but the primary endpoint (number of mature oocytes) and subjective assessments like embryo grading, follicle counts and cycle cancellation were made by unblinded investigators who knew group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the ovarian response to gonadotropin was clearly evaluated using transvaginal ultrasonogram by one investigator"

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary endpoints are pre-specified in the text, but no trial registration or protocol is cited, no sample size/power calculation is reported, and many outcomes are reported without adjustment for multiplicity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary efficacy end point was the number of mature oocytes retrieved. Secondary efficacy variables included total amount and days of rhFSH administered..."

overall_summary: This randomized trial used a computer-generated list and achieved balanced baseline characteristics with near-complete outcome data, but the open-label design (acknowledged lack of clinician blinding, no placebo gel), possible imperfect allocation concealment since the sequence was given to investigating physicians, unblinded assessment of partly subjective outcomes (mature oocyte counts, embryo grading, cycle cancellation), and absence of a registered protocol/power calculation together yield some concerns. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective, single-blinded randomized controlled trial with allocation by a computer-generated random number list ("patients were randomly divided into two groups with the help of a computer-generated random number list"), with placebo (lubricant gel) control.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence with pre-numbered identical bottles suggests adequate generation and concealment and baseline variables were balanced, but the group sizes are unequal (46 vs 41) and are reported inconsistently between the abstract (41 treatment / 46 control) and the results/tables (46 TTG / 41 control), leaving uncertainty about how allocation was actually implemented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "patients were randomly divided into two groups with the help of a computer-generated random number list. Both testosterone and lubricant gel were kept in numbered bottles with dispensing pumps for each patient according to the randomization schedule."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded by an identical-appearing placebo gel, but treating physicians (who individualized gonadotrophin dose and decided on trigger/cycle cancellation) were unblinded, and the 3 excluded control patients indicate the analysis was not strictly intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Only treating physicians were aware of the allotment (single-blinded study)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Exclusion of three control-group patients for poor response — an outcome-related reason occurring only in the control arm — could bias comparisons of oocyte number and pregnancy rates, although the proportion (6.8%) is small and Table 3 appears to use the full randomized denominators.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Three patients in the control group were excluded from the study due to poor response"

domain_judgments.rationale: Oocyte count and pregnancy outcomes are objective, but assessors/clinicians and embryologists were not blinded (only patients were), which could influence subjective judgments such as embryo grading, follicle counting and decisions to cancel cycles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary outcome has been assessed in terms of the number of oocytes retrieved in patients receiving testosterone gel pretreatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary outcome and sample-size calculation are reported, but registration appears to be institutional rather than in a public prospective trial registry with an accessible protocol, many secondary outcomes are reported, and some figures are internally inconsistent (e.g., clinical pregnancy 29.3% in the abstract/Table 3 vs 22.89% in the text), so selective reporting cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "registration of the trial with the institution bearing registration no. MCDH/2019/27"

overall_summary: This placebo-controlled, computer-randomized trial with balanced baseline characteristics raises some concerns rather than high risk: clinicians/embryologists were unblinded, three control patients with poor response were excluded (non-ITT), and the absence of a public protocol together with internally inconsistent group sizes and pregnancy-rate figures leaves scope for selective reporting. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is some concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective randomized controlled trial in which 70 eligible women were allocated to testosterone gel or standard treatment using "Computer generated random sequences... for randomization", with CTRI registration and ethics approval.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used and baseline characteristics were comparable, but no information is given on allocation concealment (e.g., sealed opaque envelopes or central allocation).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Computer generated random sequences were used for randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 70 randomized women for the primary outcome, with only one exclusion from pregnancy outcomes for a documented clinical reason (freeze-all for OHSS risk).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All women were analyzed for primary outcomes... Thus 34 patients were analyzed for pregnancy outcomes in the study group and 35 patients were analyzed in the control group

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (oocyte count, pregnancy, live birth) are objective and measured identically, but no blinding of embryologists/assessors is reported and subjective elements such as oocyte/embryo grading and cycle cancellation decisions could be influenced by knowledge of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After 34-36 hours of hCG trigger, oocyte retrieval was done and oocytes were graded according to maturity

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was unblinded with no placebo gel, so participants and clinicians knew the assignment, and gonadotropin dosing/embryo transfer decisions were made by unblinded clinicians (the study group received significantly more embryos transferred, which the authors acknowledge may explain pregnancy differences); analysis appears near-ITT (all randomized analysed for the primary outcome).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The women in control arm served as active controls and did not receive gel treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and a pre-specified primary outcome with a priori sample-size calculation is reported, but no registration number/protocol is provided for verification, many secondary outcomes are reported, the results tables are internally inconsistent (Table 2 duplicates Table 1 values), and emphasis on the "take home baby rate" (p=0.049), not listed among the pre-specified outcomes, suggests possible selective emphasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India.

overall_summary: Randomization was computer-generated with comparable baseline characteristics and essentially complete outcome data, but the trial was unblinded with no placebo gel, allocation concealment was not described, outcome assessors were not blinded, and the absence of an accessible protocol together with reporting inconsistencies and emphasis on a non-pre-specified "take home baby rate" raises selective-reporting concerns. These issues yield an overall judgment of some concerns rather than low risk.

design_rationale: Although the data source is a randomized trial, the reported comparisons (tapered vs. maintained rFSH dose, coasted vs. not coasted, hCG delayed vs. not delayed) were not randomized; they reflect clinician-determined, response-driven management within a single reference arm, analyzed retrospectively ("Retrospective analysis of data from the NA reference arm").

domain_judgments.rationale: Exposure (tapering, coasting, delaying hCG) was by definition driven by ovarian response — the groups differed markedly at the time of the decision (higher estradiol and follicle counts on day 8 in tapered patients), which is itself a strong prognostic factor for oocyte yield and pregnancy, and no adjustment or matching for these or other baseline confounders (age, BMI, AFC, indication) is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In patients tapered (<200 IU rFSH) (n¼85) vs maintained at 200 IU rFSH on day 8 (n¼283): higher serum estradiol and number of follicles on day 8 were observed

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants came from a defined trial arm (403 patients, 14 centers), which limits selection bias, but the subgroup denominators are inconsistent (85+283=368 of 403; 129+239=368), indicating unexplained exclusion of patients and post-exposure definition of groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 403 patients from 14 centers received 200 IU/d rFSH ... tapered (<200 IU rFSH) (n¼85) vs maintained at 200 IU rFSH on day 8 (n¼283)

domain_judgments.rationale: Exposure groups were defined by objective, prospectively recorded trial data (rFSH dose <200 vs 200 IU on day 8, coasting ≥1 day, hCG delayed by 1 day) and classification could not have been influenced by knowledge of the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: followed by daily rFSH (%200 IU/d) from controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) day 8 onward

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The "interventions" are themselves co-occurring protocol deviations (tapering, coasting, delayed trigger) applied non-blinded by treating clinicians, and the three comparisons overlap in the same patients with no reported handling of co-intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ganirelix acetate 0.25 mg/d was initiated on COS day 5, and hCG was given when R3 follicles reached R17 mm, or the next day.

domain_judgments.rationale: 35 of the 403 patients are unaccounted for in the compared subgroups and no information on missing outcome data or how it was handled is provided in the abstract.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 403 patients from 14 centers ... (n¼129) compared with those not coasted (n¼239)

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (oocytes retrieved, MII oocytes, ongoing pregnancy rate) are objective, were collected uniformly under the parent trial's standardized procedures, and are unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of dose-adjustment status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: more total (mean - SD: 16.8 - 7.0 vs 12.7 - 7.4) and metaphase II (MII) oocytes (12.2 - 5.9 vs 9.1 - 5.2) were retrieved; and ongoing pregnancy rates (PRs) were similar

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: This is an unregistered post hoc retrospective analysis of a trial arm with three separate exposure definitions and multiple outcomes, sponsored by the manufacturer, with no p-values, confidence intervals, or pre-specified analysis plan reported — a high potential for selective reporting of non-inferiority ("no detrimental effect") conclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Retrospective analysis of data from the NA reference arm of a large randomized, multicenter clinical trial (Engage). ... Supported by: Merck & Co. Inc

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is serious, driven by confounding by indication (tapering, coasting and delayed trigger were response-driven decisions, with demonstrably different day-8 estradiol and follicle counts between groups and no adjustment reported) and by serious risk of selective reporting in this unregistered, industry-sponsored post hoc analysis lacking p-values, confidence intervals or a pre-specified analysis plan. Exposure classification and objective outcome measurement were at low risk, but these strengths cannot offset the confounding and reporting concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes random allocation of eligible women with poor ovarian response into two testosterone gel groups and a control group: "eligible patients were randomly allocated into two TTG intervention groups (4 week and 6 week groups) and one control group through a manual lottery. Allocation concealment was by sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes."

domain_judgments.rationale: A random allocation method (manual lottery) and concealment via sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes are described, but the sequence generation is only vaguely specified and the baseline table shows an implausible, unexplained imbalance in a strong prognostic factor (prior IVF history: 14.3% control vs ~85% in both treatment arms) reported with a non-sensical P = .98, raising doubts about either the randomization or its reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "eligible patients were randomly allocated into two TTG intervention groups (4 week and 6 week groups) and one control group through a manual lottery. Allocation concealment was by sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes." … "History of IVF treatment | Yes | 6 (14.3) | 36 (85.7) | 32 (84.2) | .98"

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinicians were unblinded and controlled a key co-intervention (individualized rFSH dosing and cycle management), and the control group received no placebo gel so participant blinding is questionable, although an intention-to-treat analysis was stated and deviations/cycle cancellations were balanced across arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All participants were blinded to group assignment; however, researchers were not blinded." … "The FSH starting dose and FSH dose adjustment were based on patient's condition and individual ovarian response."

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 23% of randomized participants (37/159) were excluded post-randomization with unequal losses across arms (11, 15 and 11), analysis was effectively per-protocol despite the "intention-to-treat" claim, and reasons for withdrawal (switching to donor oocytes, quitting before stimulation) could plausibly relate to assigned waiting time/treatment and to prognosis, with no sensitivity analysis provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Among the 159 women who were eligible and agreed to participate, 37 were lost to follow-up because they received a donor egg or quit treatment before ovarian stimulation" … "randomly allocated into two transdermal testosterone gel intervention groups (53 cases in 4 wk group and 53 cases in 6 wk group) and one control group (53 cases) … results in the final data with 42, 38, and 42 women"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (oocyte/embryo counts, hCG levels, ultrasound-confirmed pregnancy) are objective and laboratory-based and were assessed identically, but outcome assessors/clinicians were unblinded and some measures (embryo morphology grading, AFC, endometrial thickness by ultrasound) involve subjective judgment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A possible limitation of this study is that it was not double-blinded as the clinicians were aware of the groups the patients were classified."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT04602143), but registration appears retrospective (2020, after the Jan 2018–Sep 2019 recruitment), no protocol is available for comparison, and multiple pregnancy outcome definitions plus post-hoc adjusted logistic models (emphasized when unadjusted differences were weaker) raise the possibility of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the registration number at Clinical trials was NCT04602143" … "Multivariable logistic regressions were used to quantify the effect of the treatment group, adjusted for all potential confounders"

overall_summary: Overall high risk of bias, driven by substantial post-randomization attrition (37/159, ~23%, excluded for reasons plausibly related to allocation and prognosis, analysed per-protocol despite an ITT claim). Additional concerns arise from a marked unexplained baseline imbalance in prior IVF history, unblinded clinicians who controlled individualized gonadotropin dosing, and likely retrospective registration with multiple outcome/analysis options.
